meta: What can humanoid robots do? They can now fold clothes, pour water and stack boxes, but still much more slowly than you. Why, how they learn, and where they work today.

muc.title: Humanoid robots
muc.text: Humanoid robots can now fold clothes, pour water and stack boxes, but they still work much more slowly than you.

muc.title: Easy for people, hard for robots
muc.text: Strangely, AI beat humans at chess long ago, yet a robot is still very clumsy at holding a soft shirt.

muc.title: See, understand, then move
muc.text: New robots use an AI model that sees through a camera, understands an instruction, then controls the hands, learning from thousands of human demonstrations.

muc.title: Where they work
muc.text: Today robots do real work mostly in warehouses and factories, where tasks repeat and the routes are familiar.

muc.title: Watch robot videos with a sharp eye
muc.text: When you watch a robot video, look for the small text saying whether it's real speed or sped up, and whether the robot works on its own or someone controls it remotely.
